paragraphs: Partage Club sells an app for sharing everyday items, and the site pitches it as a way to borrow what a household needs instead of buying it. Joining is free, and the site says a member creates a profile, finds an item nearby, requests it, and returns it. Coverage is described in terms of reimbursement up to a set amount if something happens during a share.

The homepage sorts visitors into paths for citizens, cities and municipalities, business and organization, and building your own platform. For cities, the offer is described as a fully supported, turnkey sharing solution that empowers citizens to share, save, and connect. A parallel offer aims at employees and members inside businesses and organizations. The platform option is a customized sharing platform powered by the company's technology, with infrastructure, a safety framework, and expertise supplied for deploying a sharing ecosystem tailored to an industry.

The mission page states the goal as making sharing the obvious choice so every community can unlock its collective abundance. The frequently asked questions page shows question headings for damage, late returns, giving items away, selling items, and account deletion.

quote.text: You don’t need to own it all.
